title: Sun's binomial-power q-log-convexity conjecture: m=2,3 proofs and m>=4 counterexamples
description:
For integers m ≥ 2, let Rn(m)(q) = ∑k=0n C(n+k, k)m qk and Δn(m)(q) = Rn−1(m)(q) Rn+1(m)(q) − (Rn(m)(q))2. The second part of Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 1.1(i) (arXiv:2505.02767) asserts that (Rn(m)(q))n≥0 is q-log-convex for every integer m ≥ 2.

Result. The conjecture holds for m = 2 and m = 3, and fails for every m ≥ 4. For all m ≥ 4 and n ≥ 23, the coefficient of q2 in Δn(m)(q) is strictly negative; in particular, [q2]Δ23(4)(q) = 2764 + 3254 − 2·3004 + 5754 − 5764 = −2,999,950.

This archive contains the Chinese proof notes (LaTeX sources and compiled PDFs), exact rational verification scripts using only the Python 3 standard library, and a Lean 4.19.0 / Mathlib project. The Lean development completely formalizes the disproof for all m ≥ 4, the explicit fourth-power counterexample, the q2 coefficient positivity for m = 2, 3, and selected algebraic identities from the cubic proof; the full coefficientwise positivity proofs for m = 2, 3 are in the LaTeX notes and exact rational certificates.

Earlier counterexamples by Qiping Zhou (m = 5, n = 7) and Shivam Patel (m = 4, n = 23, and eventual failure for each fixed m ≥ 4), as well as the theorem of Chen, Tang, Wang, and Yang used in the m = 2 low-degree case, are credited in the README and proof sources.
